**Asia’s Giant Softshell Turtle (Pelochelys cantorii)**

The Asian giant softshell turtle (*Pelochelys cantorii*), also known as Cantor’s giant softshell turtle, is one of the largest and most elusive freshwater turtles in the world. Distinctive for its broad, pancake-like body and smooth, leathery shell, this remarkable species can reach up to 1.8 meters in length and weigh over 100 kilograms (“Giant Softshell Turtle”). It inhabits slow-moving rivers, streams, and marshes across Southeast Asia, including countries such as Thailand, Cambodia, Indonesia, and parts of India (van Dijk). The turtle’s flattened appearance, paired with cryptic coloration, enables it to hide easily in sandy or muddy riverbeds, making sightings rare.

Cantor’s giant softshell turtles display an unusual behavior: they spend up to 95% of their lives buried in sand with only their eyes and nostrils exposed, ambushing passing prey such as fish and crustaceans (World Wildlife Fund). The species primarily feeds on aquatic invertebrates and fish, using its strong jaws to crush hard-shelled prey. Its secretive nature has contributed to the scarcity of data about its habits and population status.

Sadly, *Pelochelys cantorii* is listed as Critically Endangered on the IUCN Red List. Habitat destruction caused by damming, pollution, and sand-mining, along with overharvesting for food and the illegal pet trade, pose major threats to its survival. Conservation efforts, including habitat protection, research, and local education initiatives, are essential to halt the decline of this remarkable turtle (World Wildlife Fund; van Dijk).

The Asian giant softshell turtle’s striking appearance and unique ecological role highlight the urgency of freshwater conservation in Asia. Without focused initiatives, future generations may lose the chance to witness this extraordinary species in the wild.

---

**Photos:**

![Giant Softshell Turtle by Stuart J. Blanch](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/8/8e/Pelochelys_cantorii_SJB_1.jpg)
*Figure 1. Asian giant softshell turtle. Wikimedia Commons, Stuart J. Blanch.*

![Cantor’s Giant Softshell Turtle](https://i.natgeofe.com/n/7707a407-4255-4405-8fa5-0514fa1a0769/CantorsGiantSoftshell.jpg)
*Figure 2. Cantor’s giant softshell turtle. National Geographic.*

---

"Giant Softshell Turtle." *National Geographic*, www.nationalgeographic.com/animals/reptiles/facts/asian-giant-softshell-turtle. Accessed 1 June 2024.
